title: Composite Canary Gate: unified health mesh for private VPC canary rollouts
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Goal: Build a composite canary gating mechanism for Private (VPC) rollouts that synthesizes latency, error-rate, saturation, KV-cache health, and token throughput into a single rolling health score. This ticket implements the probe definitions, Terraform module changes, alert rules, rollout integration points, and automated rollback triggers for canaries running in customer VPCs and private edge workers.

Motivation: Existing synthetic probes are useful but siloed (latency-only / errors-only). During recent private upgrades we saw situations where a p99 latency spike was transient but combined with a 20% drop in KV cache hit-rate and rising GPU occupancy the user experience degraded over longer windows. A composite signal reduces noisy false positives while producing earlier sustained-detection for real regressions.

Scope:
- New "health-mesh" probe CRDs deployed via Terraform module (optional for customers).
- Composite health scoring operator that consumes probes and emits a composite health metric per deployment and per-zone.
- Canary gate integration with rollout controller: auto-stop and rollback when composite health breaches configured thresholds for N consecutive windows.
- Dashboard and alerting updates in Console + runbook links.
- Test harness and chaos scenarios.

Out of scope: builtin remediation beyond automatic rollback (we will provide playbook links). Full RBAC controls for customers will be covered in a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- Terraform module exposes new resource: redwood_vpc_composite_probe with clear options for weights and decay window.
- Composite health metric (redwood_vpc_composite_health{deployment,zone}) emitted at 30s resolution.
- Canary controller pauses/rolls back when composite health < 0.7 for 3 consecutive 1m windows (configurable).
- Unit and integration tests for composite operator, including synthetic load and KV-cache-drop scenarios.
- Console dashboard shows composite signal alongside raw probe components.
- Runbook created and linked in ticket.
- Security review sign-off obtained (see security_review_required).
infra_changes:
Terraform changes (module):
- module 'vpc-probes' new resource 'redwood_vpc_composite_probe' with attributes: weights (map), decay_window_seconds, emit_resolution_seconds, target_labels (deployment, zone), alerting_profile.
Example HCL snippet:

resource "redwood_vpc_composite_probe" "prod-canary" {
  deployment = "canary-2025-02"
  zone = "us-west-2a"
  weights = { latency_p99 = 0.4, errors_ratio = 0.3, kv_hit_drop = 0.15, gpu_saturation = 0.1, token_throughput_drop = 0.05 }
  decay_window_seconds = 120
  emit_resolution_seconds = 30
  alerting_profile = "sensitive-canary"
}

The module will also install a minimal sidecar to aggregate probe values if the customer opts in (opt-in flag to avoid adding agents by default).
rollout_plan:
1) Merge infra PR and operator PR to canary branch. 2) Deploy to staging VPC (internal) with synthetic workload generator. 3) Run chaos tests (KV layer drop, GPU throttling, token surge). 4) Validate composite metric and dashboard. 5) Gradual rollout to 10% of production VPCs using canary controller with composite gate enabled. 6) Monitor for 48h, then promote to full release.

Rollback criteria: composite_health < 0.7 for 3 consecutive 1m windows OR errors_ratio > 5% for 2 consecutive windows. Automated rollback implemented in controller webhook; manual rollback instructions in runbook.
monitoring_queries:
PromQL examples used by operator and dashboards:
- Latency p99 (deployment): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, deployment))
- Errors ratio: sum(rate(requests_total{status!~"2.."}[1m])) by (deployment) / sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) by (deployment)
- KV cache hit ratio (deployment): sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[1m])) by (deployment) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[1m])) by (deployment)
- GPU occupancy: avg_over_time(gpu_device_utilization_percent[1m]) by (instance, deployment)
- Token throughput: sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[30s])) by (deployment)

Composite score (operator pseudocode):
composite = clamp(1 - (w1*normalize(latency_p99) + w2*errors_ratio + w3*kv_hit_drop + w4*gpu_saturation + w5*token_throughput_drop), 0, 1)
Where normalize(latency_p99) maps latency to 0..1 using SLA baselines and tail-constrained scaling. Decay applied: composite_smoothed = ema(composite, decay_window_seconds).
alert_rules:
Alerting rules (Alertmanager-compatible YAML snippet):
- alert: VPCCompositeHealthDegraded
  expr: redwood_vpc_composite_health < 0.7
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
    team: infra
  annotations:
    summary: "Composite health degraded for {{ $labels.deployment }} (zone={{ $labels.zone }})"
    description: "Composite health dropped below 0.7 for over 3 minutes. Check dashboards and runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Composite+Canary+Runbook"

- alert: VPCCompositeStallIncreasedTokens
  expr: increase(tokens_emitted_total[1m]) > (expected_tokens_per_minute * 2)
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: warn
    team: infra
  annotations:
    summary: "Unexpected token surge for {{ $labels.deployment }}"
    description: "Token emission doubled relative to baseline. Verify traffic shaping and L7 proxies."
test_plan:
- Unit tests for scoring function and decay math.
- Integration tests: deploy operator + terraform module to ephemeral VPC in CI.
- Synthetic scenarios: (a) latency-only spike, (b) KV cache drop of 30% for 5 minutes, (c) GPU occupancy increase to 90% under sustained tokens, (d) combined scenario leading to composite < 0.6. Verify rollback behavior triggers only for sustained combined scenarios.
- Chaos run: use kube-chaos to throttle network to KV layer and verify detection.
- Post-deploy smoke: validate dashboard tile, composite metric emission, and alert routing.

notes: Trade-offs: a heavy-handed composite can mask sudden critical failures if weights are misconfigured; we mitigate this by keeping emergency error-rate overrides that can short-circuit composite (errors_ratio > 10% -> immediate page). We intentionally keep the sidecar optional to limit customer footprint. Future work: telemetry tagging for multi-tenant debugging, RBAC for composite probe lifecycle, and an SDK for customers to provide custom probe inputs.
